trades.name: Electrical
trades.blurb: IBEW apprenticeships. Cook and DuPage may sit different tests — 701 is confirmed on the Electrical Training Alliance paper, and 134 is unresolved, so both formats are provided.

blueprints.scoring: Stanine 1-9. A 4 or higher is needed to be interviewed; the score is combined with an interview score to rank applicants.

blueprints.testName: Format not confirmed — either the Electrical Training Alliance test or the GAN Aptitude Battery
blueprints.scoring: Stanine 1-9; a 4 is the minimum and Local 134 is competitive, so a 6 or higher is realistically needed.
blueprints.unverified: Which instrument Local 134 actually administers. EJATT publishes no format. Two practice exams are provided, one in each format, so preparation is covered either way. Confirm with EJATT at 708-389-1340 before relying on one.

blueprints.testName: GAN Aptitude Battery — the other possibility for Local 134
locals: IBEW Local 134 / EJATT (Cook County) — if EJATT tests through GAN
blueprints.scoring: If this is the instrument, ranking is by score as with the other GAN programs.
blueprints.unverified: Whether Local 134 uses this at all. GAN's own site lists electricians among the Chicagoland trades it tests, and EJATT hands out a study guide at registration, which fits GAN's $20 guide rather than the free ETA sample. Against that, EJATT is an IBEW+NECA trust and IBEW/NECA programs nationally use the ETA test. Both formats are provided so preparation is covered either way. Settle it with EJATT on 708-389-1340.

sharedExams.note: Local 134, GAN-format variant. This is the shared GAN battery paper. Use it if EJATT turns out to test through GAN rather than the Electrical Training Alliance — which is still unresolved, so practise both if you are applying to 134.

trades.name: Sheet metal
trades.blurb: SMART Local 73. The local publishes no test format, so this follows the GAN battery — read the caveat before relying on the timings.

blueprints.scoring: Local 73's own apprenticeship notice says only that applicants take an aptitude test and are ranked by score. A 70% pass mark is commonly reported but is not published by the local.

sections.name: Spatial Relations
sections.format: Paper folding, pick the unfolded sheet

blueprints.unverified: Everything about the format. Local 73 publishes no blueprint at all — its official notice confirms only that an aptitude test exists and that applicants are ranked by score. GAN lists sheet metal among the Chicagoland trades it tests, which is why this exam follows the GAN battery, but that is an inference. The section split and timings follow the structure UA Local 597 publishes. Confirm with the Local 73 training centre, or with the $20 GAN study guide sold at application time, before treating these timings as real.

blueprints.scoring: Applicants are ranked by score. A $20 study guide is sold by GAN at the time of application.

trades.name: Elevator constructor
trades.blurb: The EIAT. Three sections, cloze reading, and a math section with a “No answer” option.

blueprints.scoring: Pass mark 70%. The score also sets position on the eligibility list, so a higher score is called sooner.

sections.name: Mathematics
sections.format: Multiple choice, five options, last is “No answer”

blueprints.unverified: The three sections and the 35 / 35 / 30 split are confirmed against the NEIEP 2024 study guide. NEIEP does not publish per-section time limits; the 25 / 25 / 40 minute split shown here is what preparation courses consistently report, and is derived.

trades.name: Cross-trade drills
trades.blurb: Skill sets that are not tied to one trade: sign analysis (four underlying rules) and variable relationships (all four sub-types).

trades.name: Ironworking
trades.blurb: Iron Workers Local 1. The only trade here where GAN is confirmed by GAN itself selling the test registration.

blueprints.scoring: Applicants are ranked by score. Testing has been held at UIC; arrive early, bring photo ID, no late entry.
blueprints.unverified: The per-section split and timings. GAN is CONFIRMED as the testing company for Local 1 — GAN's own store sells the aptitude test registration for it — but GAN publishes no section counts or time limits for any local, so the table shown is derived from UA Local 597. Whether Locals 63 and 136 use the same instrument has not been checked.

sharedExams.note: This is the shared GAN battery practice exam. GAN administers one instrument across many Chicago-area programs, so this is the same paper the other GAN trades practise on — it is not a separate test written for this trade. The section split follows UA Local 597 and is derived.

trades.name: Sprinkler fitting

blueprints.scoring: Aptitude test plus an interview with the Training Center; $25 application fee; five-year apprenticeship.
blueprints.unverified: Everything about the format. Local 281 confirms an aptitude test is part of the process but publishes no format. It is a UA local, and the other two UA locals in this project (597 and 130) both use GAN, which is why this battery is shown — but that is an inference, not a confirmation.

trades.name: Boilermaking
trades.blurb: Boilermakers Local 1. The format reported for this trade does not match the GAN battery, so no exam is offered yet.

blueprints.scoring: Not published. Applications are taken on the third Thursday of each month at 2941 S. Archer Ave.
blueprints.unverified: The format entirely. Local 1 publishes no blueprint. Third-party prep sources describe a boilermaker exam of roughly 100 questions split into Mathematics (about 50), English and Reading (about 22) and Science (about 28) — a structure unlike the GAN battery. Because that split is third-party only and unconfirmed for this local, no full-length exam is offered here. Use the skill drills, and confirm the format with the local before relying on any practice paper.

trades.name: Heat and frost insulating
trades.blurb: Insulators Local 17. Reported as a written maths test rather than a full battery, so no full-length exam is offered.

blueprints.scoring: Reported pass mark 70%, followed by an oral interview.
blueprints.unverified: Question count, time limit and the exact topics. What is reported is that the test is a written maths aptitude test with a 70% pass mark plus an oral interview — narrower than the multi-section batteries the other trades here sit. Because it appears to be maths-only, offering a six-section battery would misrepresent it, so this trade points at the arithmetic, fractions, percent and geometry drills instead.

trades.name: Outside line construction
trades.blurb: IBEW outside line work. Same Electrical Training Alliance test as the inside wireman, with a lower qualifying score at some JATCs.

blueprints.scoring: Stanine 1-9. Some outside line JATCs qualify applicants at 3 rather than the 4 most inside programs require.
blueprints.unverified: Whether every outside line JATC uses the same two-section paper as the inside wireman programs. The section counts and timings are CONFIRMED for the Electrical Training Alliance test itself; what is not confirmed is that no outside program substitutes a different instrument. The qualifying score does differ by program.

sharedExams.note: This is the shared Electrical Training Alliance practice exam. The ETA test is one instrument used across IBEW/NECA programs, so this is the same paper the inside wireman applicants practise on. Check the qualifying score your JATC actually uses.
